subject: Autoscale/SLO qualification follow-up - FastBank (post-call recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Rivers <ellen.rivers@fastbank.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Autoscale/SLO qualification follow-up - FastBank (post-call recap & next steps)

Hi Ellen / Tom -

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can scope an autoscale/burst plan that meets FastBank's SLOs. Please correct anything I misunderstood.

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for user-facing streaming responses; p99 <= 800ms acceptable for non-streaming admin flows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~350 req/s, typical peak windows ~500-600 req/s, event bursts up to ~800 req/s for short periods (5-20 minutes).
- Concurrency: ~300 concurrent active sessions, surging to 600+ during campaigns.
- Streaming: required for chat/assistant UX (progressive tokens).
- Availability: targeting 99.9% overall; strong requirement around graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or queued responses) rather than hard failures.
- Logging/observability: need access to per-route latency histograms and token-level cost breakdown for diagnostics.

Key questions we need from your side to finalize a scope & MOP: 
1) Can you share a 48-72 hour sample traffic trace (timestamps + request size + burst windows)?
2) What are your preferred regions (we assume us-west + us-east), and any data residency constraints?
3) Is it acceptable to run an initial load test using a Redwood staging pool that mimics your production model/quantization profile?

What Redwood can offer / proposed next steps: 
- Autoscale plan options:
  Option A - Dedicated warm pool (recommended): pre-warm a pool sized for 75% of expected peak to achieve <30s serve-up for most bursts.
  Option B - Reserved + burst capacity: reserved baseline for steady-state, with on-demand burst capacity up to your peak (scale-up 60-120s depending on model/hardware).
  Option C - Hybrid with fallback: smaller cheaper model variant for degraded mode + queueing policy to keep p95 SLA for primary flows.

- We're attaching a draft SLO grid and mutual action plan to this thread for review (FastBank_SLO_grid_v1.pdf, FB_mutual_action_plan.xlsx).

Next steps (proposed):
- You: share traffic trace + confirm regions and any compliance constraints (by EOD Wed).
- Redwood: provide a sizing proposal and runbook for warm-pool sizes + expected scale-up times (by Fri).
- Schedule: 1-hour technical run-through with Dev/infra (suggest Thu 11am PT).

Happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: FastBank_SLO_grid_v1.pdf, FB_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap - that matches our notes. A few clarifications and answers to your questions below.

Traffic trace: we'll extract a sanitized 72-hr trace and upload to the Drive folder you shared by EOD Wed.
Regions: US-only for now (us-west primary, us-east failover).
Compliance: must go through FastBank's standard vendor security review (we'll share the questionnaire tonight).

SLO tolerances: we reaffirm p95 <= 300ms for streaming UX. For batch/admin calls p95 <= 1.2s is OK. We also want graceful degradation where the assistant falls back to a 2x-smaller model within 10s if warm capacity can't be reached.

Burst profile: our marketing campaigns historically spike traffic for ~10-25 minutes and then drop. Sustained peaks >20 minutes are rare but possible during large events. Expect concurrency to hit ~600 during those windows, with very short spikes to 900 in extreme cases.

Warm pools: we'd prefer the warm-pool option if it keeps the UX within p95 targets. Please include cost delta vs pure on-demand in your proposal.

I'll confirm availability for Thu 11am PT - Tom and I should be able to make that.

Thanks,
Ellen Rivers
Head of Digital Channels | FastBank
ellen.rivers@fastbank.com | (202) 555-0144

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Rivers <ellen.rivers@fastbank.com>, Tom Hargrove <tom.hargrove@fastbank.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Autoscale/SLO qualification follow-up - FastBank (post-call recap & next steps)

Ellen - perfect, thanks for the details. A few technical notes and what we'll include in the sizing proposal:

1) Warm pool sizing - recommendation: start with warm pool sized to handle ~70-80% of your 10-25 minute bursts (we'll propose a concrete GPU count after we see the trace). Warm instances are kept with model loaded and KV cache populated for the most common prefixes to reduce cold-start work.

2) Scale-up times - realistic expectations:
   - Pre-warmed instance: < 10s to serve after connection routing.
   - Cold instance (spin-up + model load): 60-120s depending on model size & quantization.
   - We can reduce cold-starts by using lighter quantized variants or snapshotting warmed KV caches.

3) Queueing & backpressure - we'll propose a multi-tier policy: short in-memory queue (configurable, default 200ms max wait), graceful fallback to smaller variant after configurable threshold (e.g., 10s), and circuit-breaker to reject requests beyond sustained overload to prevent cascading failures.

4) Streaming behavior - streaming with progressive token flush reduces perceived latency; we'll validate p95 on a streaming path during load tests since tokenization & network can add variance.

Attachments: I've re-attached the draft SLO grid and MAP. We'll include cost delta estimates for warm pool vs on-demand and a recommended test plan.

Proposed next step: 1) we'll prepare the sizing proposal + cost comparison by Fri; 2) Thu 11am PT for technical run-through (I'll invite Lukas and Dev).

--Marissa

Hi Ellen / team -

Quick technical note ahead of Thursday's run-through: 

- Queueing behavior: for streaming sessions we recommend limiting head-of-line wait to 250ms to avoid degraded UX; for non-streaming flows a slightly longer queue (up to 1s) is acceptable. We enforce request timeouts at the routing layer and propagate cancelation to the model runtime to free KV cache resources.

- Warm-pool implementation: warm pools maintain model weights + shard-local KV caches. On a failover/scale event we prioritize routing to warmed shards and use a token-aware prefix cache to reduce generation cost.

- Recommended load-test: 48hr with 3 simulated campaign spikes (10-25m) that mimic your concurrency profiles, and a couple of long tails (30-90m) to validate autoscale elasticity and cost. Please upload the trace so we can parameterize the simulator.

Action items for FastBank: share the sanitized trace + confirm test windows.

We will bring concrete GPU counts and a cost comparison (warm vs pure on-demand) to Thu's session.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
